clue.text: Family tension

definitions.meaning: a line of descent or breed, a family stock
stress or pressure, physical or mental

explanation.definitionFit: A breed or lineage is a strain, and so is the stress of overwork or a pulled rope.

clue.text: Incentive to romp in the garden

indicators.note: to here means attached onto, so the incentive is placed after the romp

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun or frolic, a romp
a spur is something that urges on, an incentive

explanation.surface: Something that encourages children to play out in the back garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a flower you would find in the garden, and the setter leans on that setting rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphinium-like larkspur is a common cottage-garden flowering plant.

clue.text: Imagine office wag reading message from Blackpool, for instance

parts.note: to picture something is to imagine it
a post is a job or position, an office
a card is a joker or wit, a wag

explanation.surface: A joker in the workplace reads aloud a holiday greeting sent from the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool is a traditional English seaside resort, the kind of place holidaymakers send greetings from; 'reading' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Holidaymakers at seaside resorts mail illustrated cards home, so a seaside greeting is an example.

clue.text: Hotpot, say, can be kept in this container

definitions.text: Hotpot, say, can be kept in this container

parts.words: Hotpot, say, can be kept in this container
parts.note: read 'hotpot' not as a stew but as a hot pot of tea, kept warm under a knitted cover

explanation.surface: A lidded dish for keeping a Lancashire stew warm.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire hotpot is a British meat-and-potato stew; the clue wants a pot that is hot, namely a teapot, kept warm by a fabric cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded fabric cover slips over a teapot to keep its brew warm.

clue.text: Grand American donuts all so hard when cooked

indicators.note: cooking something changes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American baker's ring doughnuts all turn out rock-hard in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cooked' rearranges DONUTS ALL SO HARD; 'grand' is slang for a thousand of a currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is slang for a thousand, and American money is counted in dollars.

clue.text: Measure of light excluder?

definitions.meaning: a dry measure of capacity, eight gallons
from the Bible saying about hiding your light under a container of that name

explanation.definitionFit: It is an old unit of grain volume, and the Gospel image of hiding one's light under one makes it something that shuts out light.

clue.text: Norse god of noise abatement?

parts.note: noise abated completely leaves nothing, the letter O for zero
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian deity who presides over quieting things down.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'noise abatement' as no noise: zero (O) before din.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the chief deity of Scandinavian mythology.

clue.text: Tailless animal in covered walk

indicators.note: without its tail means the final letter of the animal is cut off

parts.note: the stoat is a small animal of the weasel family

explanation.surface: An animal without a tail wanders into a sheltered colonnade.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greek architecture this is a roofed colonnade or portico for walking.

clue.text: Reverse, a girl's best friend?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Reverse, a girl's best friend? (3)': 'a girl's best friend' is diamonds, slang ICE, but no reading of 'Reverse' gives or signals ICE; the word looks misread or garbled.

clue.text: Dogs or badgers?

definitions.meaning: to badger someone is to pester or harass them

explanation.definitionFit: Hunting dogs are hounds, and to pester someone persistently is to hound them.

clue.text: A small container for a large sum of money!

definitions.meaning: a small parcel or box, as of cigarettes

explanation.definitionFit: A little box or parcel is one, and in British slang something costing a lot costs a fortune of that name.

clue.text: Herald's lying down-can't contain cry of pain

indicators.note: contain means the cry is held inside the letters of the word can't

parts.note: the letters of the word, apostrophe dropped
ouch is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A herald lying on the ground cannot stop himself crying out in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herald's' means in the language of heraldry, not a messenger; 'contain' puts the cry inside the apostrophe-free word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry an animal shown resting with its head raised is described by this term.

clue.text: Makes runs in plot perhapsthat's not cricket!

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters are just one possible arrangement, an anagram

explanation.surface: A batsman scoring runs in a field, and someone protests at foul play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MAKES RUNS IN PLOT. 'It's not cricket' is a British idiom for unfair behaviour; the page runs 'perhaps' and 'that's' together.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not cricket is a British idiom for unfair play, the opposite of fair and gentlemanly.

clue.text: Infant king I would support

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so it follows the king

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: A baby monarch with someone volunteering to back him.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is an informal word for a child or baby.

clue.text: Treatment is the right pay adjustment

indicators.note: adjusting means rearranging, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Fixing the right wage level as a cure for workplace grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: It is remedial care for an illness or a psychological condition.

clue.text: Smash success

definitions.meaning: a smash is a big success
a popular success such as a chart song

explanation.definitionFit: Both a smash and a success describe a show or record that sells hugely; smash can also mean strike.

clue.text: They increase the volume, fin ally

definitions.text: They increase the volume, fin ally

parts.words: They increase the volume, fin ally
parts.note: the volume is a book, not sound; extra material is placed at its end

explanation.surface: Things that turn up the sound level at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fin ally' is the page's split of 'finally': supplements are added at the end of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra items appended to a book are added at the back, swelling it.

clue.text: Explains powder in sex-change

indicators.note: in means the powder word goes inside the other letters
change signals the letters of sex are rearranged

parts.note: to pound something is to grind it to powder

explanation.surface: Someone describes taking a powdered hormone during gender reassignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges sex into EXS, and 'in' sets the grinding verb inside it after the first two letters; 'sex-change' looks like one compound but splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out or interpret something in detail.

clue.text: Scrap for bargain treasure

parts.note: a snip is British slang for a bargain
a pet is a darling or treasure

explanation.surface: Trading a piece of junk for something valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snip' as a bargain is everyday British slang, as in 'it's a snip at that price'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece or fragment of something is a snippet.

clue.text: Looks vacant, as does the astronaut

definitions.meaning: taken literally, an astronaut gazes into outer space

explanation.definitionFit: Gazing blankly is the idiom, and an astronaut literally peers out at the cosmos.

clue.text: Try again in court

parts.note: to try a case again before a judge

explanation.definitionFit: A retrial means hearing a case again before a court.

clue.text: Bronchitic, perhaps, from using scythe?

indicators.note: using the letters means working them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone got short of breath from swinging a scythe in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronchitis sufferer has a congested chest, and the informal adjective describes that.

clue.text: Did it go to Falstaff's head when he hit the sack?

definitions.text: Did it go to Falstaff's head when he hit the sack?

parts.words: Did it go to Falstaff's head when he hit the sack?
parts.note: Sir John Falstaff is a knight, so a knight's cap goes on his head; sack is also the sherry he drank, and a bedtime drink goes to the head

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's drunken knight goes to bed with drink on his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff is Shakespeare's sherry-loving knight; sack is his wine, and 'hit the sack' is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedtime drink, or the old cap worn in bed, both suit a knight retiring with his sack.

clue.text: Holly is one above the law

indicators.note: in a down clue, above means placed before

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: Holly is a plant that sits above any law.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus name of holly.

clue.text: Bay made half a turn that was funny to watch

definitions.text: made half a turn that was funny to watch
definitions.meaning: Stan ... was half of the comic double act ... and Hardy, a turn being a stage act

explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree is a kind of laurel, and Stan of that surname was one half of a famous comic duo.

clue.text: Remove for restoration

definitions.meaning: to ... to a place is to go or move there

explanation.definitionFit: To go off to another room is an old sense, and fixing something is mending.

clue.text: Musical perception found in the army

indicators.note: found in means the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A soldier discovers a talent for music.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a good feel for music, pitch and tune is called having one of these.

clue.text: Work-tax

definitions.meaning: a task one is obliged to do
a levy, as customs or excise

explanation.definitionFit: An assigned task is one, and so is a customs levy on goods.
